commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: fix(bridge): report models for a session this process did not create
commits.body:
Displaying an external session deliberately skips the ACP load, to avoid
starting a second agent just to show history. Config options only arrive with
that load, though, so #48 left every external session reporting no models — and
after a bridge restart every session is external, so the model box stayed on
"loading" everywhere and switching model failed, since setModel validates
against that same empty list.

Measured against real OMP 17.1.3 before the fix: a session created by this
process returned 2 providers and 6 models, one created by an earlier process
returned 0 and 0.

The ACP load now happens only when config options are genuinely missing, so
opening a session stays as cheap as #48 made it and only the model picker pays
for it. Verified that the extra load preserves the merged external history: a
four-message session was identical before and after, and switching model on it
is accepted.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: feat: name the harness in the header, and name a failed model fetch
commits.body:
Two changes from the same confusion: an app pointed at the wrong server looked
like an app with broken models.

The header showed only `host:port`, so nothing said which harness was being
driven — even though that decides what the app can do, and the same host can
serve a different one. It now carries a badge with a distinct accent per
harness, sized to match the pills already in use. The badge never shrinks and
the address truncates instead, so a long hostname cannot push it off a narrow
screen. All six harness/theme combinations were measured at 4.84:1 or better
against their own background; the OpenCode badge uses --primary-strong because
--primary on --primary-soft lands at 4.43:1, under AA for 10px bold text.

A model list that never arrived rendered as "loading configured models…"
indefinitely, which reads as a slow server rather than a failure. The error was
already held in modelLoadError and shown in the model panel, but not where it
would be seen. Every model label now goes through one value that names the
failure, and the context chip marks it. A model already known keeps showing if a
later refresh fails, since blanking it would lose good information.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: feat: mobile polish, measured at 375x812
commits.body:
Seven independent fixes from a pass over the app at phone width. Each number
below was measured in the browser, before and after.

The on-screen keyboard had no help at all. The viewport meta now carries
interactive-widget=resizes-content: without it Chrome on Android keeps the
layout at full height when the keyboard opens, so the sticky composer ends up
behind it. None of the seven fields declared a keyboard: the host field was
autocapitalised and autocorrected while typing an address, the port raised a
full keyboard, no field offered itself to a password manager, and the composer's
action key did not say send. All of them now do.

A session card was 193px tall, of which 62px was a 114-character absolute path
wrapped over three lines, and the status row wrapped over three more. The path
is shortened to its last two segments with the full value kept in the title
attribute, and "no file changes" is now said by its absence. The card is 123px
and the list went from 3274px to 2295px — twice as many sessions before
scrolling.

The composer placeholder was 69 characters in a box 217px wide: it could not be
read. It is 25 now, on one line with room to spare.

The rename pencil sat permanently at 60% opacity on touch, because full opacity
was only ever reached on hover, which a finger cannot produce. Dimming is now
inside @media (hover: hover).

Also: Android's blue tap flash no longer fights the pressed state the buttons
already have, scrolling to the end of a list no longer drags the page underneath,
and the sheet close button was the only control under 44px at 37px — compact
buttons are now thumb-sized.

Removed settings.hostHint in all three languages and the assertion covering it:
the hint it belonged to was deliberately dropped, so the strings were dead and
the test was defending them.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: fix: one honest state when the server cannot be reached
commits.body:
Found by looking at the app with the bridge stopped, which is what a phone sees
whenever it loses Wi-Fi or the workstation sleeps. It showed four hopeful
messages and a developer-facing error at the same time, for about ten seconds:

  Connessione e caricamento sessioni...
  Riconnessione aggiornamenti live…
  Connessione al backend
  Carico le sessioni. Su mobile o dopo il risveglio del server...
  ✗ Network error: cannot reach http://127.0.0.1:4097/session. Check server
    hostname/port, Windows firewall, and CORS (--cors).

Three separate status surfaces each spoke for themselves, so the app both
claimed to be loading and reported failure. It now settles into one state in
255ms, measured: the reason, and the two actions worth offering.

Tolerating three failures before admitting defeat protects a working list from a
hiccup, but on the first load there is nothing to protect — it only delays the
truth while an error is already on screen. One failure with an empty list is now
enough.

The event stream no longer says it is reconnecting while the connection itself is
down, the raw transport error no longer repeats what the offline state already
explains, and New session is disabled rather than offered when it cannot work.

The transport error also spoke of Windows firewalls and --cors, the latter
meaningless inside the app where CORS does not exist. It is now the host and
port, with the CORS note only where it can apply.

This is also the answer to a real question it provoked: the app does not cache
sessions. A reload with the server down shows an empty list. What looked like a
cache was in-memory state that a failed refresh left untouched — which is why
sessions opened empty, and why the list is no longer presented as usable.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: feat: fix the session header, and rebuild the rename affordance
commits.body:
You were right that I had been measuring the list and not the view you were
looking at. Two defects in the session detail, both measured.

The header still carried the full absolute path plus a timestamp with seconds,
107px over three lines — the same problem I had shortened in the cards and left
here. It is 56px now, with the path shortened to its last two segments and the
full value in the title attribute.

Below the messages sat the note explaining that a session came from another
client, at y=631 to 649, while the sticky composer starts at y=642: eight of its
nineteen pixels were behind the composer, so it read as half a sentence. It is
now a pill in the header, with the full explanation as its title.

Rename was a 14px pencil in a 37x44 button, not square, dimmed to 60%, placed
with an inline style inside an h2. The title itself is the button now — 142x44
instead of 37x44, with an 18px pencil as the hint rather than the target.

The editor asked the user to guess which of two unlabelled 14px glyphs commits.
Save is labelled and disabled until the name actually changes; cancel is a
square icon button with an accessible name.

Two assertions needed rewriting rather than satisfying, both because they pinned
the shape of the code rather than what it guarantees — the same trap the
contributing guide warns about. One required `selectedSession?.external` to
appear verbatim, when what matters is that an external session stays marked and
explained. The other required a specific hover block that no longer exists; it
now checks that no interactive control starts dimmed on a touch device.
